title: I may not like HULK all that much, but I certainly admire Ang Lee's ambition to make something more than just a basic action movie.

commenti.body: I actually do like Hulk all that much.  There's some goofy stuff, there's some stuff I don't think works, but man, what a joy to watch a superhero movie that's more concerned with its characters and their trauma than it is with smashin' stuff--and the way smashin' stuff actually intertwines with its characters in ways that are more than just "uh oh, here's a dangerous situation, guess I gotta do this thing I don't like..."

Haven’t seen it in years but I love it and have a fond connection with that movie. 

It’s also unofficially the first MCU movie because the Norton movie was a loose sequel. 

Well, I guess Spider Man 1 now is tied with the MCU as well.

I loved all the fight scenes and still think the dogs are kinda scary. His last battle with absorbing dad is still a highlight in any superhero movie. Incredibly abstract and feels like something you’d see in Twin Peaks as opposed to anything being made today. 

Eric Bana remains my definitive Hulk

Ang Lee is an amazingly versatile director. Let’s not forget he directed an incredible adaptation of “Sense and Sensibility” in 1995, and then came up with a masterpiece like “Crouching Tiger…” just a few years later. He moved swiftly between a British period piece and a martial arts movie because those were established genres where his fresh take could be recognized. With “Hulk”, superhero movies didn’t have a distinctive identity as its own genre. That’s not to say he would benefit from a formula like the MCU later established. That’s just to say that, IMO, his directorial choices didn’t seem as cohesive or justified. 

There was an attempt to emulate comic book language with split-screens, there was the conception of action sequences that honestly couldn’t be successfully executed with the visual effects available at the time, there were too many conflicting elements in terms of tone and narrative for the movie to work either for its target audience or niche viewers. That's my opinion, of course. I think Hulk is a mess, but I appreciate a mess way more than a soulless, by-the-book adaptation.

Oh absolutely! He's an acclaimed director for a reason. SENSE AND SENSIBILITY is a movie I always watch whenever I catch it on tv. I'm a big fan of his movies in general and I can't wait for Bruce Lee biopic. One thing that you can definitely tell with LIFE OF PI is how much he improved when it comes to gimmicky editing (even if it's not as overdone in that film as HULK).

And regardless of what one might think of HULK, there's no denying that you still feel his passion in every single frame. The fact that he put on the motion capture to play Hulk is very commendable and speaks volumes about how much he cared about the project.

I think he's a filmmaker that takes creative risks, and that's admirable. That means he's also prone to fail, because he plays outside of a comfort zone. Hulk is a misfire, but a respectable misfire. It's not the result of lazy choices.
